summary:
# NOTES: THE DATCHET DIAMONDS (Richard Marsh; Gutenberg #40353; illus. Stanley L. Wood; frontispiece "Shall I shoot all three of you?" p.265)

## CHARACTERS
- **Daisy Strong (Miss Strong)**: heroine. Mother dead; mother left her £120/yr. Lives Medina Villas, Brighton, with Charlie.
- **Cyril Paxton (Mr. Paxton)**: Daisy's fiancé; City speculator ("punter"), gambler; lost on Eries; bought 10,000 Trumpit Gold Mine shares.
- **Charlie / Charlotte Wentworth (Miss Wentworth)**: 30, Daisy's friend and housemate; journalist (writes for *Fashion* etc.), earns >£500/yr; pince-nez; sharp, mocking.
- **Mr. Lawrence** = **Reginald Hargraves, alias "The Toff"**: fair, blue eyes, pink-white complexion, soft penetrating whisper; met Daisy at Devil's Dyke (umbrella in rain, April). Thief. Proposes to Daisy.
- **The Baron** = **Isaac Bergstein**: German-American; tall, thin, stooped, long black overcoat, oversized top hat, dirty-red complexion, beady black eyes, vulture nose, huge mouth, no chin, talon-like finger; nasal twang; fires revolver.
- **Stephen Eversleigh**: duchess's manservant, short-sighted, prized spectacles (duke's birthday gift).
- **John Ireland**: Scotland Yard detective (inspector); grey stubbly beard; shrewd brown eyes.
- **Mr. Franklyn**: lawyer, ~40, grey-streaked black hair, grey-black eyes; friend/adviser of Cyril and Daisy; holds Cyril's Trumpit shares in strongbox.
- **Skittles**: Lawrence's henchman; short, pail of water, chloroform, branding-iron; ugly, bristled, big ears.
- **Bill Cooper**: undersized, ragged informer; "Tom the Toff" and "the Baron" did the theft.
- **George Hollier**: police officer assigned to shadow Franklyn, later guard.
- **Treadwater**: manager of Makell's Hotel; clerk with curled moustache.
- **Duchess of Datchet** (young, beautiful); **Duke of Datchet**.

## BOOK / CHAPTER NOTES

**Ch I – Two Men and a Maid (Brighton pier)**
- Waltz danced earlier at Dome Masonic Ball: Daisy danced 5x with Lawrence; Charlie 2x.
- Daisy meets Paxton; Paxton asks "Where's Charlie?" Charlie at home finishing copy for *Fashion*.
- Paxton: "going for the gloves" (last Eries bull; "win you or lost you for ever"). Eries falling. Trumpit Gold Mine loss.
- Daisy: if he loses, must end; "we must be as strangers." Emigrating next week. Kiss; meet tomorrow evening on pier.

**Ch II – Overheard in the Train**
- Paxton, first class, new brown Gladstone; to Southampton, American line.
- Evening paper: "ROBBERY OF THE DUCHESS OF DATCHET'S DIAMONDS! AN EXTRAORDINARY TALE." Diamonds worth ≥£250,000. Duchess carried them to Windsor (Queen's guest); left by 4:05 train; box with Eversleigh; bank (Bartlett's Bank); Grosvenor Square; box found empty.
- Paxton peers through pivoting glass into next compartment; sees Lawrence & German-American; opens glass half-inch, listens.
- Overheard plot: Eversleigh's spectacles photographed; duplicate case; at Windsor Station booking-office stranger says "Have you lost your glasses?"; Eversleigh swapped box (rug trick); Lawrence took real box by South-Western line.

**Ch III – The Diamonds**
- Brighton refreshment-room: Lawrence greets Paxton ("Mr. Paxton, I believe"); Paxton leaves by cab to Makell's Hotel.
- Gladstone lock stiff; finds ring, tiara hidden in shirts; bag not his (Lawrence's brown bag swapped).
- Gems: Datchet Tiara, Begum's Brooch, Banee's Bracelet, Amsterdam Necklace (~£100,000).
- Hides stones in newspaper inside bag; leaves bag; goes to Daisy.

**Ch IV – Miss Wentworth's Rudeness**
- Daisy waits at pier gates; Cyril late. "I know all about it" (papers).
- Cyril claims chance of £250,000. Daisy proposes marriage "within a month"; quotes Ruth ("Whither thou goest").
- Charlie: sneering; "one will almost begin to wonder... if you can have come by them honestly." Paxton storms out; Daisy calls him honest.

**Ch V – In the Bodega**
- Lawrence & Baron confront Paxton at Bodega: "What was the colour of your Gladstone bag, eh?" Paxton lies (says black, old).
- Paxton admits losing bag in refreshment-room; they leave.
- John Ireland approaches. Hints he knows where diamonds are; "white elephant"; warns "it's a lifer." Asks Paxton to bet; Paxton declines.

**Ch VI – The Adventures of a Night**
- Paxton followed by two men (Number One, Number Two). Deposits bag with Makell's manager.
- Smoking-room stranger questions him (room number); porter says he took a bed.
- Night: burglar fails with nippers at door; then ladder at window in fog; dark lantern flashed; Paxton fires revolver (kept under pillow). Men flee; ladder and lantern left behind.

**Ch VII – Placed in Safe Custody**
- Morning: Paxton rents safe at Chancery Lane Deposit Company; deposits diamonds; Pullman to town.
- Shadowed by cigar-smoker in billycock; Paxton has constable hold him. At London Bridge, two men and a countryman (pretend accident) try to rob him.
- Papers: 3% on £500,000 = £15,000/yr.

**Ch VIII – In the Moment of His Success**
- Paxton has ~£200 left; drinks; returns to Makell's.
- Manager: shabby man claimed Paxton sent him for bag ("Medina Villas", a shilling each); refused.
- Evening paper City article: Trumpit shares £10. Paxton bought 10,000 shares ~2 yrs earlier (failed; unsaleable). Now ~£100,000 worth.
- Leaves for Daisy; struck from behind, chloroformed, bundled into cab.

**Ch IX – A Proposal of Marriage**
- Daisy waits 20 min past time on pier; quarrelled with Charlie that day.
- Lawrence on pier (mackintosh): claims he saw Paxton in town at Criterion bar, staying in town. Proposes to Daisy; she says she is engaged to Paxton. Lawrence: "you will learn that I have cause for sorrow."
- Daisy home; tells Charlie; Charlie: "Mr. Lawrence... introduced by his umbrella." Daisy weeps. Knock: Mr. Franklyn.

**Ch X – Cyril's Friend**
- Franklyn: Trumpit shares now £12 10s (closed); 10,000 shares in his strongbox; Cyril major holder. Needs Cyril's authority to sell.
- Franklyn offers to find Cyril; Daisy: "within the hour."

**Ch XI – John Ireland's Warrant**
- Franklyn had heard from acquaintance that he saw Paxton leave Victoria for Brighton. At Makell's, Paxton out. Franklyn leaves card: "I shall be at Medina Villas till eleven."
- Ireland: warrant for Paxton, robbery of Datchet diamonds. Bet: £100 at evens that Paxton "has guilty knowledge" (Franklyn takes bet; note in Ireland's pocket-book).
- Ireland shows ring dropped from Paxton's handkerchief outside Makell's.
- Ireland orders Hollier to shadow Franklyn; cabs with police.

**Ch XII – A Woman Roused**
- Hollier at Medina Villas door; Franklyn tells Daisy about warrant. Daisy furious; scorns Franklyn; dismisses Charlie ("never again I'll call you friend"). Franklyn & Charlie accompany Daisy to Makell's.
- Daisy tells Hollier: "I am Daisy Strong, Mr. Cyril Paxton's promised wife."

**Ch XIII – The Detective and the Lady**
- Ireland at Makell's: "Inspector Ireland"; search warrant (blue); strong-room letter lock. Bag opened: nothing valuable. Manager: Paxton took valuables to London.
- Daisy confronts Ireland; grabs bag; Ireland leaves Hollier.
- Bill Cooper: "Tom the Toff" did the nicking; "the Baron" put him up; wants "ten thick 'uns" to go to 'Merriker. Daisy promises £50. Cooper: Paxton captured by Toff and Baron; taken to a "crib."
- Ireland + Daisy + Cooper cab to police station.

**Ch XIV – Among Thieves**
- Paxton wakes, bound, soaked; Skittles ("Lord Mayor and Aldermen"); chloroform cloth; kidnapped.
- The Baron enters; Paxton: "you'll be hanged." Baron shoots near his ears (singes lobe), grazes cheek.
- Paxton's wrists burned; fires shots.

**Ch XV – Put to the Question**
- Lawrence (Toff) enters with two men. Explains theft ("I appropriated the Duchess's diamonds"); mentions he "chanced to meet a certain lady" and was rivalled by Paxton. Demands diamonds; Paxton refuses ("I will never tell you").
- Orders branding-iron marked "thief."

**Ch XVI – A Modern Instance of an Ancient Practice**
- Skittles brands Paxton's right shoulder-blade; Paxton breaks free, takes iron, hits Skittles on head.
- Baron fires and misses; Paxton clubs Baron (hat crushed); Paxton seizes revolver.
- Lawrence blows whistle; Paxton's gun clicks empty (Lawrence had counted shots: "six-chambered").
- Paxton clubs Lawrence unconscious; sets lamp to burn; flees into pantry-like cupboard with window; shouts "Help!"; answering "Hollo!"

**Ch XVII – The Most Dangerous Foe of All**
- Overheard: men flee, leaving Baron and others in burning house.
- Paxton's escape hopeless; writes will on scrap of notepaper: "I give and bequeath all that I have in the world to my dear love, Daisy Strong, who would have been my wife. God bless her!—CYRIL PAXTON."

**Ch XVIII – The Last of the Datchet Diamonds**
- Ireland's waggonette (Cooper, sergeant, dozen constables) stops fly on road; three captured; two men lying in fly.
- Burning house: Daisy finds Paxton's hand at window; will falls; she drags him out.
- Weeks later Paxton wakes at Miss Wentworth's house; policeman guards him.
- Paxton confesses everything; diamonds recovered from Chancery Lane safe. Duchess gladdened.
- Trial: Reginald Hargraves (Lawrence/Toff) and Isaac Bergstein (Baron): 20 years penal servitude each; others shorter terms. Paxton a Crown witness; Cooper also a witness.

**Ch XIX – A Woman's Logic**
- Paxton sells Trumpit shares at high; invests in consols; vows no more gambling.
- Paxton and Daisy married quietly at a Brighton church after trial.
- Daisy's "feminine logic" in quarrel over his "unworthiness"; reconciliation.
- Final line: Paxton: "God grant that I may never again be led into such temptation!"
